placements.why: The directives command erasure of organizational knowledge artifacts — a decision and a migration knowledge domain — naming an organizational category for governing what knowledge is carried versus purged. No existing strata or narrative leaf covers knowledge lifecycle management.
placements.title: From Knowledge Accumulation to Lifecycle Stewardship
placements.frame: What knowledge does the organization retain, deprecate, or erase, and who directs that lifecycle?

placements.title: From Carrying Knowledge to Commanding Its Erasure
placements.frame: What knowledge does the organization direct to be forgotten or removed, and what scope does that erasure claim?
placements.why: Both segments are terse imperatives commanding the elimination of specific organizational knowledge — a decision ('Forget the Quantum Widget Decision') and an entire knowledge domain ('Remove all knowledge about the PostgreSQL to QuantumDB migration'). They share a matter-of-fact register, authority-ranking stance, and decision-level conviction, all projecting an irrealis future state of erasure. No existing leaf holds this theme.
